identity.title: The VLA/ALMA Nascent Disk and Multiplicity (VANDAM) Survey of Perseus Protostars. VI. Characterizing the Formation Mechanism for Close Multiple Systems

paper_type_evidence.quote:
We present Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations of
multiple protostar systems in the Perseus molecular cloud previously detected by the
Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA).

question.value: Are close (<600 AU) protostellar multiple systems in Perseus formed by disk fragmentation or turbulent fragmentation, judged from circum-multiple dust and gas kinematics?

evidence.quote:
definitive evidence in favor of disk fragmentation would be finding
them embedded within a common, circumbinary/multiple structure that has Keplerian rotation.

This paper
makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00031.S.

We observed 17 close ( _<_ 600 AU separation)
multiple systems at 1.3 mm in continuum and five molecular lines

evidence.loc: 4.2.3 Which is the Most Common Mechanism?
evidence.quote:
The
raw numbers indicate that for multiples on scales _<_ 600 AU, _∼_ 67% form via disk fragmentation and
_∼_ 33% form via turbulent fragmentation.

The resultant noise in the 1.3 mm continuum was
_∼_ 0.14 mJy beam _[−]_ [1]

findings_qualitative.value: Class I systems show no circum-multiple dust; most Class I have little gas emission

evidence.quote:
Most of the less-embedded Class I systems in our sample do not show circumbinary dust or
gas emission.

findings_qualitative.value: L1448 IRS3A and Per-emb-8 identified as strong disk candidates

evidence.quote: We identified two additional strong disk candidates, L1448 IRS3A and Per-emb-8.

claims.hypothesis: Close multiples form via disk fragmentation in rotating circum-multiple structures
claims.experiment: ALMA 1.3 mm continuum and five lines toward 17 VANDAM close multiples; compare velocity gradients with outflow PAs
claims.result: 8 of 12 systems have gradients orthogonal to outflow; 8 of 9 Class 0 have circum-multiple dust
claims.finding: Disk fragmentation is an important mechanism, but fractions are upper limits and statistics are small

evidence.quote: Our results suggest that disk fragmentation via gravitational instability is an important formation mechanism for close multiple systems

We conclude that the VANDAM multiplicity
detections from Tobin et al. (2016b) had very high reliability.

claims.result: S/N insufficient to fit rotation curves

evidence.quote:
The short observations presented here
do not have the S/N to robustly fit a rotation curve that can distinguish Keplerian rotation from
other velocity profiles.

why_this_method.value: ALMA provides simultaneous dust continuum and molecular lines to test circum-multiple structure and rotation

evidence.quote: ALMA enables simultaneous observation of both dust continuum to look for circummultiple structure and molecular lines to search for rotation signatures

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Inward migration of initially wide turbulent-fragmentation companions could mimic disk fragmentation; so 66% is an upper limit

evidence.loc: 4.2.3 Which is the Most Common Mechanism?
evidence.quote:
could be rephrased to say that 66% is an upper
limit on the frequency disk fragmentation for the production of close multiples.

limitations_admitted.value: Short observations give low S/N per channel; phase unstable giving ~0.1 arcsec position offsets

evidence.quote:
there are

limitations_admitted.value: Mass uncertainties from opacity, isothermal assumption, dust-to-gas ratio

evidence.quote: We caution that the masses calculated may have systematic uncertainty

referee_caveats_inferred: Orthogonality criterion (30 deg) with no statistical test; subjective moment-map PA measurements
Rotation vs infall/outflow/filtering not distinguished without PV or Keplerian fits
Single 3-minute snapshot per source; spatial filtering affects extended emission
